entity.concept: Entity is a business object; its identifier is a key, its dimension describes it.
entity.business_example: A customer buys two orders in the north region.
entity.failure: Counting order rows as customers reports two customers.
entity.question: What business object are you counting?
entity.fix: Use the Customer canonical identity, not the Order row count.
entity.recall: How do entity, identifier and dimension differ?

identity.concept: Identity mapping is a business and Modeling contract; string equality is not identity resolution.
identity.diagram:
guest email -> explicit identity map <- CRM account_id
                              |
                         customer_id
identity.business_example: One person checks out as a guest and later registers.
identity.failure: COUNT(DISTINCT email) disagrees with COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id).
identity.question: Are these records proven to represent the same customer?
identity.fix: Request an explicit identity mapping with ambiguity policy; preserve unresolved identities.
identity.recall: Why can a technically unique email still be the wrong customer identifier?

grain.concept: Grain states what one row represents.
grain.diagram:
Order $100 -> Item A $100
           -> Item B $100
           -> Item C $100
grain.business_example: One order has three product items.
grain.failure: Summing the repeated order total reports $300.
grain.question: What does one row represent before and after the join?
grain.fix: Use an order-grain fact with unique order_id; reject item fanout and ask Modeling for approved allocation.
grain.recall: Which relationship can multiply an order-level measure?

dimension.concept: A dimension describes a slicing attribute with an explicit relationship and time behavior.
dimension.business_example: An order is sliced by the customer region at the supplied snapshot.
dimension.failure: A duplicate Customer dimension row doubles joined revenue.
dimension.question: Is the right-side identifier unique, and is the attribute current or historical?
dimension.fix: Validate N:1 identity/cardinality; declare current_snapshot and require a separate SCD contract for historical slicing.
dimension.recall: Why does adding a descriptive dimension sometimes change a metric?

measure.concept: A measure is a numerical fact with an aggregation; a metric adds governed meaning.
measure.diagram: gross_order_value -> SUM + eligibility + time + owner -> gross_revenue
measure.business_example: Order value is 10000 USD cents before refunds.
measure.failure: An analyst calls the raw amount column net revenue.
measure.question: Which business decisions are missing from the measure?
measure.fix: Define a metric contract with population, grain, unit, recognition time and accountable owner.
measure.recall: What converts a measure into a governed metric?

metric.concept: A metric answers a named business question under an explicit contract.
metric.diagram: modeled data -> owner meaning -> versioned metric -> BI/API/AI
metric.business_example: Finance asks for recognized value after refunds; Growth asks for booked value.
metric.failure: Both reports use the label Revenue while serving different decisions.
metric.question: Must these decisions share one number or retain different explicit names?
metric.fix: Obtain owner decisions; define separate gross/net or booking/recognition metrics when the meanings differ.
metric.recall: Why does a larger number not establish which metric is correct?

ownership.concept: Business ownership approves meaning; technical ownership maintains execution.
ownership.diagram:
Finance -> business definition
Platform -> interface reliability
ownership.business_example: Finance chooses recognition time; Platform maintains the query tool.
ownership.failure: A Platform engineer silently chooses paid_at as revenue time.
ownership.question: Who has authority over the business decision?
ownership.fix: Record accountable business approval and technical maintenance separately.
ownership.recall: Can a passing Platform test approve a Finance definition?

time.concept: Reporting time requires event field, timezone, calendar and refund attribution.
time.diagram: created_at / paid_at / fulfilled_at -> owner decision -> timezone date
time.failure: Two valid queries group the same event into different days.
time.question: Which event and local reporting date does this decision require?
time.fix: Record the owner-chosen event, named timezone, calendar and an explicit half-open window.
time.recall: How do event time, processing time and reporting date differ?

lineage.concept: Lineage traces declared data and metric dependencies to consumers.
lineage.diagram: orders_raw -> stg_orders -> fct_orders -> gross -> net -> dashboard/AI
lineage.business_example: A refund aggregate is subtracted from fulfillment-cohort value.
lineage.failure: A metric omits the refund asset in its dependency metadata.
lineage.question: Can you trace every part of the formula to a modeled asset?
lineage.fix: Require source bindings for measures and dimensions; retain definition/source fingerprints in results.
lineage.recall: Does declared lineage prove operational freshness?

versioning.concept: A semantic revision must preserve historical interpretation and require migration.
versioning.diagram: v1 meaning -> explicit change + owner review -> v2 -> consumer migration
versioning.business_example: An order count switches from fulfillment date to created date.
versioning.failure: The same ID/version now returns different historical periods.
versioning.question: Would an old consumer interpret the new value the same way?
versioning.fix: Create a new major version for breaking meaning, effective date and migration; retain v1 explicitly.
versioning.recall: What must a consumer pin besides the metric name?

consumer_consistency.concept: Every consumer requests one governed metric/version and carries result provenance.
consumer_consistency.diagram: dashboard A / dashboard B / API / AI -> net_revenue@1.0.0
consumer_consistency.business_example: An AI tool returns the same net contract and amount as a dashboard.
consumer_consistency.failure: An LLM substitutes SUM(raw_orders) and guesses the meaning.
consumer_consistency.question: Does the response show which owner-approved definition actually ran?
consumer_consistency.fix: Accept only metric/version/window/dimensions; reject caller formulas and return definition/catalog/source fingerprints.
consumer_consistency.recall: Why does the AI language model not own the canonical business meaning?
